name: Palms — curated world set
status: 5 archetypal species (full list archived in docs/plant_archive)
notes: The recognisable palms of every palm region: tropical coasts, oases, African savanna and swamp, Asian monsoon plains and rainforest, Australia and NZ, Andean cloud forest (the wax palm as an emergent), Amazon floodplain and swamp, the SE US, desert canyon oases, the Mediterranean, and cold-hardy hill palms. Tiers: emergent for the wax palm, canopy for trunked palms, shrub for trunkless and clumping palms, epiphyte for rattan (climbing). The 'palm' shape exists; Phase 6 should give it fan vs feather crowns, a clustering form, and the doum fork.

emergent.name: Andean wax palm

growth.juvenile_note: The first seedling leaves are narrow undivided or two-lobed blades; for decades the young palm is a stemless rosette of stiff pinnate leaves, silvery-white beneath, on the shaded cloud-forest floor while the trunk base thickens underground. Only after roughly half a century does the smooth, wax-coated whitish trunk start to rise.
growth.source: Wikipedia Ceroxylon quindiuense (45 m, rarely 60 m; fruit 1.6-2 cm orange-red; minimum reproductive age ~80 yr); Sanin & Galeano 2011 Phytotaxa (Ceroxylon revision); long stemless phase and growth rate estimated from Andean wax-palm demography studies

canopy.name: Coconut palm

growth.juvenile_note: The husked nut lies on the sand and after 2-6 months a pointed shoot pushes out of one end while the nut's flesh feeds the seedling. First leaves are entire, stiff, strap-like blades split only at the tip (bifid), in a stemless fan-like rosette; pinnate fronds come later, and a trunk rises after ~3-5 years, widening from a bulbous base ('bole').
growth.source: Wikipedia Coconut (tall palms bear at 6-10 yr, live 60-100 yr; ~11 months from female flower opening to harvest; up to 15 inflorescences/yr; ~80 nuts/yr, up to 150; nut ~1.4 kg; largely cross-pollinated, dwarfs selfing); ICRAF Agroforestree (tall selections 24-30 m, flowers after ~6th yr); germination from FAO coconut guides

canopy.name: Date palm
canopy.origin: North Africa and the Middle East

growth.juvenile_note: Remote germination: the cotyledon stalk pushes the growing point down into the soil, then grass-like, undivided strap leaves emerge. For several years it is a stemless, spiny fountain of increasingly pinnate, stiff, grey-green fronds, often with suckers (offshoots) at the base, before a rough trunk clad in old leaf bases rises.
growth.source: Wikipedia (to 30 m, slow-growing; fruits 4-8 years after planting, commercial yields at 7-10; offshoots fruit 2-3 years earlier than seedlings; lives 100+ years when maintained); FAO date palm manuals (remote germination, undivided first leaves); height-age estimated from trunk growth

canopy.name: Doum palm

growth.juvenile_note: Remote-tubular germination: the cotyledon stalk drives the growing point 60-80 cm down into the soil, so the first sign is a single strap-shaped, pleated leaf. Stiff grey-green fan leaves follow from year 2-3, forming a stemless tuft for well over a decade (it may start fruiting while still nearly stemless); the trunk then rises and later forks into two, four or more crowns.
growth.source: PROTA via Palmpedia and ICRAF Agroforestree (germination 1 month to 1 year, cotyledon stalk buries shoot to 60 cm, first leaf strap-shaped, fan leaves from yr 2-3, stem after 18-20 yr in the wild, first fruit after 6-8 yr, slow growth); hyphaene.org (to 80 cm deep, first fork 2.5-4 m). Lifespan estimated.

canopy.name: Moriche palm

growth.juvenile_note: The seed sends a germination tube down into the wet soil from which the seedling rises. The first leaves are simple, strap-like pleated blades; later leaves turn into huge rounded costapalmate fans on long stalks. For years it is a stemless tuft of fans in the swamp while the trunk base thickens underground, then a smooth grey column rises and old leaves fall cleanly away.
growth.source: Wikipedia Mauritia flexuosa (to 35 m, flowers Dec-Apr, scaly chestnut fruit with yellow pulp, seeds float and are spread by floods and fish); palm establishment and growth rates estimated from Mauritia/Neotropical fan-palm literature
